description: The bar chart illustrates the number of participants who selected each criterion when evaluating a generative-AI-driven claim retrieval system, as reported in the paper “A Generative-AI-Driven Claim Retrieval System Capable of Detecting and Retrieving Claims from Social Media Platforms in Multiple Languages.” The vertical axis lists seven evaluation criteria: “Relevant FCs,” “FC Summary,” “Relevance Explanation,” “Clarity and Simplicity,” “Overall Summary,” “Filters,” and “Veracity Explanation,” arranged from top to bottom in descending order of participant count. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” ranges from 0 to 6 with tick marks at intervals of 2. Each criterion is represented by a horizontal bar with a distinct color: “Relevant FCs” (dark purple, 6 participants), “FC Summary” (dark blue, 5), “Relevance Explanation” (teal, 3), “Clarity and Simplicity” (green, 3), “Overall Summary” (light green, 2), “Filters” (lighter green, 1), and “Veracity Explanation” (lime green, 1). The bars are sorted in descending order of participant count, with “Relevant FCs” being the most selected criterion and “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” tied for the least selected. The chart visually emphasizes the relative importance participants placed on different aspects of the system’s output, with functional components (FCs) and summaries receiving the highest attention.
